note: [agent-bulk] numucc_em. THIS EVENT CARRIES NO CLUSTERING JUDGEMENT - the verdict is a PID statement and is silent on whether the grouping is right (correction 6). Vertex judged from the native r95 framing (event_half_span_cm 115.8, below the 150 cm re-capture threshold): the blue star sits at the base of a bundle of three or four near-parallel tracks leaving one way and a ~35 cm track leaving the other; it is a real convergence and I am NOT calling it vertex-bad. shw 14028 (301.9 MeV, pdg 11, 2 segments, len 42.2) is not an EM shower, on four grounds. (1) SHAPE: on both az-055-el+20 and az+085-el+20 it is a perfectly straight, uniformly MIP-narrow line for its whole 42 cm - no apex, no cone, no branching, no widening at either end. (2) It is the far half of ONE continuous straight track: below the shower start X the SAME line continues, in the same direction, as unowned grey charge - 14027, tagged pdg 13, 70.0 cm, reading dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 against 14028. So the reconstruction has cut one straight through-line into a 70 cm grey muon and a 42 cm 'shower'; start/axis wrong is the right phrase for where that X sits. (3) The shower's own body is hadron-tagged: 38038, the 37.8 cm segment that carries nearly all its length, is pdg 2212 in the reconstruction's own particle id, taken in by pass3_cone at 3.4 cm / 19.0 deg; the 14028 seed itself is only 4.4 cm. (4) CHARGE DENSITY: 301.9 MeV over 42.2 cm of narrow track is about 7 MeV/cm, roughly three times minimum ionising - that is a stopping-proton profile, not a 300 MeV electron, which at 42 cm (three radiation lengths) would be visibly showering. Context that supports all of this: the vertex bundle 14026 (pdg 211, 36.4 cm), 14041 (pdg 211, 28.7 cm) and 14022 (pdg 211, 13.0 cm, explicitly walk_excluded) are ALL correctly left grey, so the reconstruction kept the other hadrons out and promoted this one. If it IS somehow an EM shower, then nothing is missing from it - every unowned segment is either behind it (143-175 deg) or a 2.4 cm stub at 46.7 deg (32034) - and the only questionable inclusion is the 38038 proton itself. pi0: showers[].pio_id is -1, no group accepted, only one shower above 20 MeV in the event, no pairing to dispute; the kine_pio_* line (mass 39.8 from E2 = 8.5 MeV) is the BDT feature over all candidate pairs and is not a pairing. Not looked at: the 10 showers the scope rule skipped, all under 20 MeV min_kine_best.
